name: Brimble Sandboxes

plans.name: Hacker
plans.note: Includes 5 sandbox CPU-hours + 10 GB-hours per month; usage above is metered ('Sandbox CPU / memory | Metered above plan-included sandbox allowances') at an unpublished rate. Plan fee does NOT include app CPU/RAM.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Includes 20 sandbox CPU-hours + 40 GB-hours per month (brimble.io/pricing 2026-09-28); overage rate not published. Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $11 per seat per month, min 1 seat; same allowances as Developer (15 concurrent sandboxes, 20 sandbox CPU-h + 40 GB-h).

caveats: Public paid-plan sandbox quotas. PaaS bandwidth/object storage rates are not automatically sandbox snapshot/egress rates; no sandbox overage CPU/RAM unit price established.

ENGINE_CARD cannot apply all independent free CPU/RAM/storage/request allowances exactly. Raw regimes/worked example retain them; any engine subtotal may overstate charges or miss eligibility. Do not subtract them twice.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Re-checked 2026-09-28: pricing page publishes plan fees, concurrency, max runtime and included CPU-/GB-hours only; no per-resource or overage rate, so the card stays unpriced.

Brimble app/project compute is $1/vCPU-month and $1/GB-month (~$0.0014/h, region multipliers e.g. 1.45x) but the docs explicitly exclude sandboxes from that page; do NOT use these as sandbox overage rates.

Snapshots expire: each has expires_at set by plan-dependent retention; an hourly reaper deletes expired snapshots. Snapshot storage bills while held ('Metered above plan-included snapshot allowance').
Auto-destroy timers only 30m/1h/3h/6h/12h/18h plus a platform max-lifetime ceiling; spending limit with action 'pause' rejects every new sandbox create until raised or the cycle rolls.

Sandbox size conflict: docs (paper.brimble.io/sandboxes/overview) cap sandbox memory at 2 GB and scratch disk at 1-5 GB, but the pricing page advertises up to 2 vCPU / 4 GB (Hacker) and 4 vCPU / 8 GB (Developer). A 4 vCPU / 8 GiB sandbox may not be creatable.
Free plan: the pricing page says "Sandboxes available on paid plans", but the docs say free accounts get "a small sandbox quota" in free-marked regions only. Contradictory, so not modelled as a plan.
One-time 14-day Developer trial for eligible personal accounts; a payment method is required before it starts (paper.brimble.io/billing/plans).

fleet.tiers: Hacker 3 simultaneous sandboxes; Developer 15; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Sandbox concurrency, not build concurrency (separate 1/2 builds). 50/300/1,000 not established by published self-serve plans; CPU shape sizes are not aggregate quotas.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: RAM state, running processes, and open sockets never survive a pause regardless.
snapshot_auto.note: Pause scales the container to zero and keeps only the persistent workspace volume; no state capture on pause/destroy/auto-destroy. There is an opt-in cron-scheduled snapshot mode (snapshotMode: automatic + snapshotFrequency), filesystem only, which skips ticks while paused - scheduled backups, not stop-triggered snapshots.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can launch a brand-new sandbox from any snapshot you own, with exactly the files you saved.
snapshot_on_demand.note: SDK/API/dashboard snapshots.create on a ready sandbox; filesystem only (no memory); restore = new sandbox via fromSnapshot, any number of times (template/fork-like). Snapshots expire per plan retention (hourly reaper), not downloadable.

harness_api.quote: adjust the binary name in the exec command
harness_api.note: claude-code, codex, opencode and droid templates come preinstalled (agent_harnesses), but they are driven only through generic exec (e.g. `claude --print`) plus streamed exec / tail -f of logs; no agent-specific prompt/session/resume API in the SDK or OpenAPI.

egress_allowlist.quote: Default deny, with an allowlist of IPv4 addresses, CIDR ranges, or hostnames.
egress_allowlist.note: Modes open (default) / deny_all / restricted (max 50 entries), set at create or PUT /sandboxes/{id}/egress at runtime; sandbox-system.md: allowlist 'enforced at the host firewall for the container's address'.

egress_http_rules.quote: Each entry is an IPv4 address, CIDR range
egress_http_rules.note: Egress policy schema is only mode + allow list of IPv4/CIDR/hostname; no method/path/header rules.

ingress_rules.note: Sandboxes expose no inbound ports or preview URLs at all (only Brimble API exec/files reach them; docs say use a web service if you want a public URL), so there are no ingress controls - but also nothing public. Web-service projects have edge/internal networking, out of scope for the sandbox card.

guest_firewall.quote: Linux capabilities are stripped on the container.
guest_firewall.note: gVisor container (runsc) with capabilities stripped and no-new-privileges; no CAP_NET_ADMIN, so in-guest iptables/nftables should not take effect. Not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Sandboxes don't bake env vars into the template; you set them per-exec.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) are passed as per-exec env vars and enter the sandbox; no credential-injecting proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: pre-provisioned once, attached to a sandbox or a web-service project when you need it.
volume_attach.note: `sandbox`-type volumes 10-50 GB, region-pinned, backed by Brimble object storage (CSI), mounted at the workspace directory; attach via volumeId at create or persistent:true.

volume_shared.quote: One volume, one workload at a time. No concurrent reads from multiple sandboxes or projects.
volume_shared.note: Single-writer attachment; no multi-attach, read-only or RW.
